basis_pattern: original_plus_bounded_search. EO 10488 (signed 1953-09-23; 18 FR 5699; official Federal Register text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_10488.txt, read in full) is a single paragraph: it orders that the purchase, custody, transfer or sale of foreign exchange by any executive department or agency be administered under regulations issued by the Secretary of the Treasury, and authorizes the Secretary to issue them. Identity: heading, title and date agree with the register row. Own terms: the order states no end date or ending condition. Later instruments: a search of the held order texts for the number 10488 finds only the order's own Federal Register copy, the 1989 codification snapshot and the held current CFR texts (31 CFR 281.1 and the part 281 authority line); no later order amends, revokes or supersedes it, and the dossier chain lists no event. Current law: the eCFR (point-in-time search as of 2026-10-14 and the GovInfo bulk copy amended through 2026-10-15) prints 31 CFR 281.1 as issued under 'Executive Order No. 10488, 18 FR 5699, 3 CFR 1949-1953 Comp.' and the part 281 authority citation names E.O. 10488 beside E.O. 10900; the section 281.1 lead is confirmed at the cutoff by the point-in-time search. The U.S. Code scan (release point 119-121, current through 2026-10-09; laws of 2026-10-10 to 2026-10-14 not reflected) has no note that prints or names this order. The order mentions section 1415 of the Supplemental Appropriation Act, 1953 (31 U.S.C. 724) and section 1313 of the Supplemental Appropriation Act, 1954 only as laws its regulations must not contradict, not as the authority it rests on (it rests on the Constitution and statutes and the President's office); the current Code text of those sections is not held and I do not assert how they now read. The three selected machine searches (current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr, later-events:ofr_catalog) were read with their coverage notes; none carries a coverage warning and none records a revocation or supersession of EO 10488.

Sec tio n 1. There is hereby established a Defense Meritorious Service Medal, 
with accompanying ribbons and appurtenances, for award by the Secretary of Defense 
to any member of the Armed Forces of the United States who has rendered outstanding 
non-combat meritorious achievement or service while assigned to the Office of the 
Secretary of Defense, the Organization of the Joint Chiefs of Staff, a specified or 
unified command, a Defense agency, or other such joint activity as may be designated 
by the Secretary of Defense.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Section 1 establishes the Defense Meritorious Service Medal for award by the Secretary of Defense to members of the Armed Forces of the United States for outstanding non-combat meritorious achievement or service in joint assignments. EO 13666 (2014-04-18) amended it to extend eligibility to members of the armed forces of a friendly foreign nation; the clause continues, amended, with no end date, so it is operative on 2026-10-14.

Sec. 2. The Defense Meritorious Service Medal, with accompanying ribbons and 
appurtenances, shall be of appropriate design approved by the Secretary of Defense 
and shall be awarded under such regulations as the Secretary of Defense may pre­
scribe, These regulations shall place the Defense Meritorious Service Medal in an 
order of precedence after the Medal of Honor, the Distinguished Service Cross, the 
Defense Distinguished Service Medal, the Distinguished Service Medal, the Silver Star 
Medal, the Defense Superior Service Medal, the Legion of Merit Medal, and the 
Bronze Star Medal, but before the Meritorious Service Medal.

THE PRESIDENT 57945
[3 1 9 5 -0 1 ]
Executive Order 12019 _ • November 3, 1977
Establishing the Defense Meritorious Service Medal
By virtue of the authority vested in me as President of the United States of 
America, and as Commander in Chief of the Armed Forces, it is hereby ordered as 
follows:
Sec tio n 1. There is hereby established a Defense Meritorious Service Medal, 
with accompanying ribbons and appurtenances, for award by the Secretary of Defense 
to any member of the Armed Forces of the United States who has rendered outstanding 
non-combat meritorious achievement or service while assigned to the Office of the 
Secretary of Defense, the Organization of the Joint Chiefs of Staff, a specified or 
unified command, a Defense agency, or other such joint activity as may be designated 
by the Secretary of Defense.
Sec. 2. The Defense Meritorious Service Medal, with accompanying ribbons and 
appurtenances, shall be of appropriate design approved by the Secretary of Defense 
and shall be awarded under such regulations as the Secretary of Defense may pre­
scribe, These regulations shall place the Defense Meritorious Service Medal in an 
order of precedence after the Medal of Honor, the Distinguished Service Cross, the 
Defense Distinguished Service Medal, the Distinguished Service Medal, the Silver Star 
Medal, the Defense Superior Service Medal, the Legion of Merit Medal, and the 
Bronze Star Medal, but before the Meritorious Service Medal.
Sec . 3. No more than one Defense Meritorious Service Medal shall be awarded, 
to any one person, but for each succeeding outstanding meritorious achievement or 
service justifying such an award a suitable device to be worn with that medal may be 
awarded under such regulations as the Secretary of Defense may prescribe-
Sec . 4. The Defense Meritorious Service Medal or device may be awarded 
posthumously and, when so awarded, may be presented to such representative of the 
deceased as may be deemed appropriate by the Secretary of Defense.
T h e W h it e H ouse ,
November 3, 1977.
